smells.finding: All three scripts are ~60 lines of undecomposed module-level straight-line procedure (read artifact, print, append to `problems`, exit). g4_assert_discharged.py in particular runs spine-status, receipt-shape, journal-verb and subprocess-re-run checks in one unbroken body with no functions.

override.repo_standard: global-crew.md: 'Make the minimal change that satisfies the handoff; no speculative abstraction.' + global-everyone.md: 'One canonical path; no speculative abstraction.'
override.reason: These are single-use command checks the engine runs once and the transcript quotes verbatim; their read surface is a top-to-bottom transcript, not a call graph. Decomposing a 60-line one-shot assertion into helpers would hide the execution order that the transcript's value depends on, and buy reuse that will never occur (each script is deleted-in-place after archive). The standard subordinates the smell because the cost the smell predicts -- comprehension load from a long body -- is not paid here: the body IS the evidence artifact.

smells.finding: No classes in the diff at all.

All three scripts repeat the same skeleton verbatim: `ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]`, a module-level `problems = []`, a print-then-conditionally-append idiom per assertion, and an identical `if problems: print each FAIL; sys.exit(1)` / else print a single uppercase sentinel tail. Three copies of a harness is textbook duplication.

The doctrine names exactly this trade and rules against the abstraction. The duplication is also self-limiting: three fixed copies, never extended.

smells.finding: Each script reads only artifacts it names directly (its own spine, receipt, journal, git OIDs). No object reaches through another's internals for data it should own.
The recurring (ROOT, WORK_ID) pair appears as module constants in each script rather than being threaded through signatures; with no function boundaries there is no clump to travel.

Findings are accumulated as a bare list of pre-formatted strings (`problems.append("substitute %r is not hash-pinned" % ...)`) rather than a typed finding value, so severity, subject and message are fused into one primitive.

override.repo_standard: ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT.md Evidence And Verification Map: evidence is reporting, not durable tooling; global-crew.md 'minimal change'.
override.reason: The strings have exactly one consumer -- stdout, read by a human in a transcript -- and are never filtered, sorted or dispatched on. A value object would add structure with no reader, which is the speculative generality the doctrine forbids. The smell predicts a cost (callers parsing primitives) that has no caller here.

smells.finding: The only function defined anywhere in the diff is `git(*args)` in g4_assert_closeout.py, a one-line varargs subprocess wrapper.

The scratch work-id is hardcoded independently in each of the three scripts (`WORK_ID = "g4-scratch-run"` in two, the literal path in the third), so re-pointing the evidence at a different work area is a three-file edit with no single point of truth -- and a partial edit would leave one script silently asserting against a stale, absent work area, where several of its checks degrade to trivially-satisfied rather than failing loudly. Raised as an OBSERVATION only, not a blocker: the scripts are archived one-shot artifacts that will never be re-pointed, so the change-amplification the smell predicts cannot actually be incurred.
Each script has exactly one reason to change (its own plan item's claim). No file mixes unrelated axes of change.
Access depth stays at one or two hops (`spine["tasks"]["context"]["status"]` is dict indexing into a document the script owns, not a navigation chain across objects).
Nothing is built for a hypothetical second caller: no flags, no config, no extension points. The scripts do one job each and hardcode everything else.

MOST SIGNIFICANT SMELL IN THE DIFF, and it is the one that matters for this issue specifically. g4_assert_discharged.py's docstring promises the check asserts 'the orientation receipt records a DEGRADED verdict', but the implementation is `degraded = "DEGRADED" in json.dumps(receipt).upper()` -- a whole-document substring scan. The structured verdict IS read one line earlier (`verdict = receipt.get("verdict") or receipt.get("status") or ""`) and then DISCARDED, used only inside the failure message it can no longer trigger. The receipt's `escalation` field is agent-authored free text, and the escalation actually passed at g4 contained the word 'degraded' ('...every Commander run in this repo is structurally degraded until a map exists'), so the assertion is satisfied by the agent's own prose. Demonstrated: a synthetic receipt with `verdict: RESOLVED` carrying that same escalation still evaluates the check to True. The printed line 'receipt degraded: True' quoted as evidence in g4-result.md is therefore produced by a substring match on agent-authored text, not by the verdict. The docstring is doing the work the code does not -- deodorant in its precise Fowler sense. OBSERVATION, not a blocker: the property is over-determined by stronger, independently-reproduced lines in the same run (orient printed DEGRADED-NO-MAP at exit 10; verify-orientation printed DEGRADED-NO-MAP; the same script's `verify-orientation re-run exit: 0` is genuinely load-bearing, which I proved by mutation R-B), so no conclusion in the result is wrong. Reported because it is exactly the #300 failure class this gate exists to hunt, appearing inside the gate's own evidence.
